reads_as_reason: Near-untapered pill-shaped columns with a flat diagonal chop at the knee and rippled, noisy zebra reflections read as a rough loft prototype, not a finished product shell.

G1.evidence: Front view shows thigh and shank as uniform rounded-rectangle bars with only a faint knee bulge. P8a 0.788 and P8b 0.807 (both failed) agree. No calf or thigh muscle-line taper, so it reads as a pill or bone, not an adult limb.

G2.evidence: Thigh-to-shank transition is a flat diagonal planar cut (side and back views), not a designed recess or flowing joint. The zebra views are broken and rippled with pinches at the knee and ankle, so the form does not flow.

G3.evidence: Colour is not rendered. The geometry has no distinct recessed band or step at the knee where a dark joint would sit, only a gap and a chamfer.

G4.evidence: Thigh and shank ends share similar rounded-rectangle sections and corner radii. The sharp planar wedge on the shank top and the uneven bulges break that family of soft radii. Not enough to call it either way.

G6.evidence: No references supplied; judged from general knowledge of Optimus and electric Atlas legs. Those have a clear taper and a defined knee housing. Here the column has near-constant width and an undefined knee. Only the soft rounded-rectangle sections loosely match.

top_changes.change: Make the thigh and shank taper clearly: cut the distal thigh and ankle sections, mostly in depth, so area ratios move toward 0.65 and 0.6; keep the widest point near the top.
Replace the flat diagonal chop at the shank top with a rounded knee cap or a clear recess; stagger the thigh distal and shank proximal stations so the gap reads as a deliberate joint groove.
Remove ripples and pinches that break the zebra bands: fewer stations, monotone w and d, same n across neighbours; keep the grey inside the red target outline.

notes: No baseline and no reference images, so no pairwise verdict. Dark joint colour not rendered. The silhouette panel's title text overlaps the shapes. (The critic read the W1 value 0 in the metrics as 'wall 0': it is a FAIL flag, not a thickness.)
